questions.question: What should you do with roof hatches on buses?

options.text: Lock them in a partly open position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lock them in a partly open position.
questions.explanation: You can lock some roof hatches partly open for fresh air, but do not do this regularly. Opening hatches will increase the bus's height slightly.

questions.question: What is the thin layer of ice that forms on roads called?
questions.explanation: Black ice is clear and thin. You can see the road through it. A road with black ice looks wet. Be careful when it is freezing and the road looks wet.

questions.question: How do you test hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brakes three times. Then press firmly on the pedal for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
Pump the brakes three times. Then press firmly on the pedal for five seconds. The pedal should move slowly toward the floor.
Pump the brakes three times. Then press firmly on the pedal for five seconds. The pedal should rise slowly.
Pump the brakes three times. Then press firmly on the pedal for five seconds. The pedal should be easy to push to the floor.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brakes three times. Then press firmly on the pedal for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
questions.explanation: Pump the brake pedal three times. Then press hard and hold for five seconds. The pedal should not move. If it moves, there may be a leak.

questions.question: When you start a vehicle, what should the coolant temperature do?
questions.explanation: After you start the engine, the coolant temperature should rise slowly toward the normal operating range.

questions.question: How can you reduce distracted driving?

options.text: Only worry about physical distractions, not mental ones.
Pre-program your radio stations while driving.
Eat while driving to stay alert.

questions.explanation: Do not have difficult or emotional conversations while driving. Pre-program radio stations before you drive. Do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving. Mental distractions can be as dangerous as physical ones.

questions.question: What should you do if another vehicle is tailgating you?
questions.explanation: Create more space in front of your vehicle so the tailgater can pass. Speeding up will not help because the driver will tailgate at the higher speed too, making it more dangerous.

questions.question: What should you do if your coolant level is low?
questions.explanation: Check your oil level, coolant level, and windshield washer fluid. Your engine needs enough coolant in both cold and hot weather.

questions.question: Is driving at night harder than driving during the day?
questions.explanation: Night driving is harder because it is difficult to see hazards, headlight glare affects your vision, and more tired drivers are on the road.

questions.question: When making a tight turn, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use your mirrors because they distract you.
Use your mirrors, but not very often.

questions.explanation: You need to know what is around you at all times. Check your mirrors regularly, especially when merging, changing lanes, turning, or making tight turns.

questions.question: What happens if you start a left turn before reaching the center of an intersection?

options.text: You will likely complete the turn safely.
The left side of your vehicle may hit other vehicles.
Other drivers will move their vehicles for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left side of your vehicle may hit other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Reach the center of the intersection before you start turning left. If you turn too early, your vehicle's path may curve left and hit another vehicle.

questions.question: What is hydroplaning?

options.text: It usually happens when driving faster than 65 mph.
It can happen with just a little water on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can happen with just a little water on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when your tires lose grip on the road and slide on a layer of water. You do not need much water for this to happen. Hydroplaning can start at speeds as low as 30 mph.

questions.question: Black ice is:
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it. It looks like a wet road. Watch for black ice if the road looks wet and the temperature is below freezing.

questions.question: When traveling downhill, a vehicle will:

options.text: Travel at the same speed as on flat road.

questions.explanation: Gravity causes your vehicle to go faster when going downhill. Slow down before you reach a downhill section so you don't have to use your brakes too much.

questions.question: Which driver is NOT a hazard?

options.text: A driver who does not scrape ice off the windshield
A driver of a station wagon with items blocking the back windows
A person driving a pick-up truck

questions.correctAnswerText: A person driving a pick-up truck
questions.explanation: Drivers with blocked vision are hazards. This includes drivers with ice on windshields, drivers with large items blocking windows, and drivers of rental trucks who are not used to the limited rear visibility. Simply driving a pick-up truck is not a hazard by itself.

questions.question: When backing with a trailer, you should:

options.text: Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the turn first.
Turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction of the turn first.
Turn the wheel as sharply as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction of the turn first.
questions.explanation: With a trailer, turn the steering wheel the opposite way from where you want to go. Once the trailer starts to turn, turn the wheel the other way to follow the trailer. This is different from backing a straight truck.

questions.question: When going down a steep hill, shift to a lower gear:

options.text: After you have already started the hill.
As far down the hill as possible.

questions.explanation: Shift to a low gear before you start going downhill. Gravity will make your vehicle go faster on hills, so be prepared.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens most often when:

options.text: A vehicle is traveling faster than 60 mph.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning is most likely when driving on wet roads with low tire pressure and worn tire tread. Hydroplaning can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water on the road.

questions.question: If you don't know how to handle a fire, you should:
questions.explanation: If you are not sure how to put out a fire, wait for firefighters. Let them handle it. This is especially important with fires involving hazardous materials.

questions.question: A driver should always:
questions.explanation: While driving, look ahead for hazards. Make a plan for how to handle emergencies before they happen.

questions.question: Cargo in a trailer:

options.text: Does not need to be secured.
Should be stacked no higher than three feet.
Should be secured to prevent movement during transport.
Should have the heaviest items on top of lighter items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be secured to prevent movement during transport.
questions.explanation: Cargo must be properly secured so it does not move while the vehicle is moving. Loose cargo is dangerous to you and other drivers on the road.
